notes: Method caveat: www.aisafetybook.com (and safe.ai/grokipedia mirrors) were blocked by this environment's network egress proxy, so pages could not be fetched directly. Content was reconstructed from (a) search-engine snapshots of aisafetybook.com/virtual-course, /curriculum, /textbook, /syllabus and /facilitate, (b) the textbook's source repository github.com/centerforaisafety/AISES (cloned; exact chapter/section headings extracted from its HTML files), and (c) the official CAIS YouTube lecture series. Course structure per the virtual-course page: an 8-week discussion phase (2-4 hrs/week of assigned readings, lectures and short assignments plus a weekly 1.5-hr facilitated cohort call) followed by a 4-week personal project phase; total ~5 hrs/week, free of charge. The first week of the discussion phase is 'AI Fundamentals Week' (textbook Chapter 2), which students with significant ML experience may request to skip. A dated week-by-week syllabus exists but is only available via an email-gated form at aisafetybook.com/syllabus, so it is not public; the mapping of the remaining chapters to sessions 2-8 above follows the textbook/lecture ordering (official Lectures 1-8 map one-to-one onto Chapters 1-8), with AI Fundamentals moved to Week 1 as the site states. IMPORTANT: the public curriculum page ('Content for Curriculum') assigns ONLY textbook chapters plus the accompanying lecture videos, slides and quizzes per chapter (some marked WIP/Coming Soon) — no external papers are publicly assigned alongside the chapters, so the reading list is the textbook itself plus the lecture videos. The full textbook is also published as arXiv:2411.01042 ('Introduction to AI Safety, Ethics, and Society', Dan Hendrycks, Taylor & Francis 2024/2025, ISBN 9781032869926); Chapter 1 closely corresponds to the standalone paper 'An Overview of Catastrophic AI Risks' (Hendrycks, Mazeika, Woodside 2023, arXiv:2306.12001), which is why that arXiv ID is attached to it. Appendix B's deep-link slug could not be verified, so it points to the table of contents; all other textbook URLs were confirmed via search snapshots of the site. An earlier course iteration described on safe.ai used 9 discussion weeks; the current site says 8 + 4.
